newsitem.title: USA: Goldman ups dlr forecasts to 1.80 marks, 130 yen.
newsitem.headline: Goldman ups dlr forecasts to 1.80 marks, 130 yen.

text.p: Goldman, Sachs and Co Inc has revised its dollar forecasts higher, citing "amazing" U.S. economic strength and an "odd" absence of Japanese intervention to slow the greenback's rise.
The dollar now is expected to fetch 1.80 marks and 130 yen in three months, the firm said in its latest edition of The Weekly Analyst dated April 15.
"We have revised our forecasts higher for the dollar over the next one and three months, although we have kept our six and 12 month forecasts basically unchanged," Goldman said.
The investment bank said it upped its three-month projections from 1.71 marks and 121 yen. It also raised its dollar/yen forecast in the one-month horizon to 129 from 124.
Two primary reasons were stated for the revisions, the first being "the remarkable strength of domestic demand indicators in the U.S."
The second was the absense of BOJ intervention, Goldman said.

"The break of 125 yen, and the lack of immediate intervention to attempt to discourage (dollar) buyers is really quite remarkable, in view of the February G7 meeting and the huge number of statements that have followed from Japanese officials ever since," it continued.
At 1145 EDT/1545 GMT on Wednesday, the dollar was trading at 1.7284/89 marks, up from its U.S. open at 1.7245/50 marks. It stood at 125.74/84 yen, barely changed from 125.77/87.
